summary: Decompose ChangeBrief into eleven independent property-level Gherkin Scenarios covering add/sub/mul/div/remainder, zero-divisor named domain errors, and single-slot memory (start zero, clear, add, subtract), with checkable HTTP/API and module surfaces required by acceptance_of_whole.
acceptance_of_whole:
Scenario: Calculator service covers ops, zero-divisor failures, and memory
  Given the arithmetic calculator service for clients
  When clients exercise add, sub, mul, div, and remainder plus single-slot memory clear/recall/add/subtract
  Then successful ops return mathematically correct numeric results for valid inputs
  And division or remainder by zero fails with a named domain error rather than an opaque language error
  And memory starts at zero and clear/recall/add/subtract update the single slot as specified
  And the HTTP/API surface and module contracts make these behaviors checkable
  And no auth, multi-user memory, or history features are required

human_gate.reason: ChangeBrief scope is explicit with empty open_questions; property-level Scenarios map one-to-one to in_scope items without blocking ambiguity.

items.intent: Support addition so clients receive the mathematical sum of two operands via a checkable service surface.
items.acceptance_criterion:
Scenario: Addition returns the sum of its operands
  Given a calculator service available to clients
  When the client adds two numbers
  Then the result equals the mathematical sum of those operands
items.scenario_name: Addition returns the sum of its operands

items.intent: Support subtraction so clients receive the mathematical difference of two operands via a checkable service surface.
items.acceptance_criterion:
Scenario: Subtraction returns the difference of its operands
  Given a calculator service available to clients
  When the client subtracts one number from another
  Then the result equals the mathematical difference of those operands
items.scenario_name: Subtraction returns the difference of its operands

items.intent: Support multiplication so clients receive the mathematical product of two operands via a checkable service surface.
items.acceptance_criterion:
Scenario: Multiplication returns the product of its operands
  Given a calculator service available to clients
  When the client multiplies two numbers
  Then the result equals the mathematical product of those operands
items.scenario_name: Multiplication returns the product of its operands

items.intent: Support division with a non-zero divisor so clients receive the mathematical quotient via a checkable service surface.
items.acceptance_criterion:
Scenario: Division returns the quotient of its operands
  Given a calculator service available to clients
  And a non-zero divisor
  When the client divides one number by another
  Then the result equals the mathematical quotient of those operands
items.scenario_name: Division returns the quotient of its operands

items.intent: Support remainder (modulo) with a non-zero divisor so clients receive the mathematical remainder via a checkable service surface.
items.acceptance_criterion:
Scenario: Remainder returns the modulo of its operands
  Given a calculator service available to clients
  And a non-zero divisor
  When the client takes the remainder of one number divided by another
  Then the result equals the mathematical remainder of those operands
items.scenario_name: Remainder returns the modulo of its operands

items.intent: Fail division by zero with a named domain error observable at the service boundary, not an opaque language or runtime error.
items.acceptance_criterion:
Scenario: Division by zero fails with a named domain error
  Given a calculator service available to clients
  When the client divides by zero
  Then the operation fails with a named domain error
  And the failure is not an opaque language or runtime error
items.scenario_name: Division by zero fails with a named domain error

items.intent: Fail remainder by zero with a named domain error observable at the service boundary, not an opaque language or runtime error.
items.acceptance_criterion:
Scenario: Remainder by zero fails with a named domain error
  Given a calculator service available to clients
  When the client takes the remainder with a zero divisor
  Then the operation fails with a named domain error
  And the failure is not an opaque language or runtime error
items.scenario_name: Remainder by zero fails with a named domain error

items.intent: Ensure single-slot calculator memory starts at zero and recall returns that initial value.
items.acceptance_criterion:
Scenario: Memory starts at zero
  Given a fresh calculator memory
  When the client recalls memory
  Then the recalled value is zero

items.intent: Support clearing the single-slot memory so subsequent recall yields zero.
items.acceptance_criterion:
Scenario: Memory clear yields zero on subsequent recall
  Given calculator memory holds a non-zero value
  When the client clears memory
  Then recalling memory yields zero
items.scenario_name: Memory clear yields zero on subsequent recall

items.intent: Support add-to-memory so the single slot increases by the given addend.
items.acceptance_criterion:
Scenario: Add-to-memory increases the single slot by the addend
  Given calculator memory holds a known value
  When the client adds a number to memory
  Then recalling memory yields the previous value plus that number
items.scenario_name: Add-to-memory increases the single slot by the addend

items.intent: Support subtract-from-memory so the single slot decreases by the given subtrahend.
items.acceptance_criterion:
Scenario: Subtract-from-memory decreases the single slot by the subtrahend
  Given calculator memory holds a known value
  When the client subtracts a number from memory
  Then recalling memory yields the previous value minus that number
items.scenario_name: Subtract-from-memory decreases the single slot by the subtrahend
